newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets end week with strong tone.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets end week with strong tone.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* NZ debt holds onto early gains to finish with firm tone
* TWI strength major driver, bonds helped by U.S. rally
* May FPI data seen positive for June qtr inflation outlook
New Zealand debt securities held onto most of their early gains to finish the week with a strong tone on Friday.
The currency's Trade-Weighted Index, which opened nearly 30 basis points higher at 67.9, eased back during the session to finish eight points higher at 67.72.

The TWI's overnight gains were cited as the main reason for a 16-basis point rally in the 90-days at the open. Despite the slip back in the TWI during the session, the 90-days managed to hang onto 13 points of their rally, to close at 6.89 percent.
The front futures contract rallied 15 basis points to 92.23 on solid volume of 5,181 contracts.
